person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: which hemisphere sustains which mathematical function, and how that division changes from infancy to school age
span.quote: The aim of this article is to summarize the state of the art about the lateralization of math functions, including its development under the influence of growth and education. In this last respect, existent meta-analyses will be scrutinized in terms of lateralization. The sources of evidence are lesion cases and neuroimaging techniques in adults as well as in developmental populations.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The right hemisphere does not simply offer its support when calculation requires generic space processing, but its role can be very specific.

span.label: hemispheric lateralization of math functions
span.quote: The aim of this article is to summarize the state of the art about the lateralization of math functions, including its development under the influence of growth and education.

span.label: review
span.quote: This corpus of knowledge is reviewed here.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: The sustained activation of the right IPS and the incremental takeover of the left inferior parietal areas eventually change into a more bilateral pattern observed in adults (see above sections).

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Thus, the interhemispheric connection seems to play an important role in the maturation of numerical representations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: Areas in the frontal, insular and occipital cortex are also recruited in these tasks and might be related with effortful control, learning and generally less automatized processing mechanisms compared to adults

span.label: the type of error left by stimulation identifies which hemisphere produced the answer: table-substitution errors after right disruption mean the left hemisphere took over, approximation errors after left disruption mean the right hemisphere did
span.quote: Disruption on right parietal areas provoked multiplication errors, mostly consisting in replacing the correct solution with another table solution (e.g., 8×3 = 32 or 8 × 3 = 16). The authors attributed this effect to the left hemisphere, where the retrieval of tables is supported, taking over the operation. In contrast, disruption of the left hemisphere resulted in approximation errors (e.g., 8 × 3 = 25). This would be due to the activity of the right hemisphere, where approximation takes place.

span.label: the right parietal lobe is proposed to store the operation-specific spatial layout that guides written multiplication, learned at school
span.quote: For example, he added the carry to the leftmost side of the multiplicand, or of the partial product, or to the partial product in the row below. He seemed to know when and how the carry must be added but he clearly forgot where . The authors concluded that he was lacking knowledge of the visuo-spatial layout representation specific to multiplication, that is learned at school and guides written multiplication.

span.label: the right insula and its surroundings support the parsing and empty-slot structure needed for numbers containing zero
span.quote: Reading aloud and writing on dictation multidigit numbers containing zero has also been found to be a right hemisphere specific function ( Benavides-Varela et al., 2016 ). Surprisingly, right hemisphere patients, who are free from language disorders, committed many errors in these tasks, and not in numbers that do not contain zero. No relation was found of such errors with neglect or with generic cognitive impairment. These errors seem to reveal the existence of a basic mechanism entailing parsing and the ability to set-up empty-slot structures required for processing zeros in complex numbers. As also confirmed in a subsequent study on a huge group of stroke patients ( Haupt et al., 2017 ), this ability can be located in the right insula and its surroundings.

span.label: the sustained activation of the right IPS together with an incremental takeover by the left inferior parietal areas turns the early pattern into the bilateral one seen in adults
span.quote: The sustained activation of the right IPS and the incremental takeover of the left inferior parietal areas eventually change into a more bilateral pattern observed in adults

span.label: the right PSPL is engaged for visuo-spatial attention rather than quantity, and may be recycled into arithmetic during education
span.quote: Unlike for the IPS, the right PSPL is not considered to be specific to quantity-based processing, but to mechanisms of visuo-spatial attention, which might be progressively engaged or “recycled” in these tasks during arithmetic education

span.label: Subtraction and multiplication could not be meta-analysed in children for want of studies.
span.quote: Because studies focusing on subtraction and multiplication are sparse, they did not provide enough statistical power for the analyses.

span.label: fMRI studies of children under 6 were excluded from the meta-analysis.
span.quote: fMRI studies with younger children were excluded because they are scarce ( Cantlon et al., 2006 ; Park et al., 2014 ; Kersey and Cantlon, 2017 ).

span.label: Correlational analyses with other variables were dropped because measures were too heterogeneous across studies.
span.quote: All correlational analysis with other variables were not considered, given the variability in measures across studies.

span.label: Hippocampal lateralization during arithmetic fact learning remains unresolved in the literature reviewed.
span.quote: The lateralization of the response in the hippocampus, however, has not been clarified in the literature.

span.label: The function of the insular and cingulate activations found for symbolic material is not established.
span.quote: More studies should address the exact function of these areas both in calculation and numerical quantity processing.

span.label: subtraction and multiplication had too few child studies to analyse, so only addition could be meta-analysed
span.quote: Because studies focusing on subtraction and multiplication are sparse, they did not provide enough statistical power for the analyses. Thus, only addition problems were analyzed. To achieve further homogeneity, only studies that involved neuroimaging (fMRI) on school-age children over 6 years were included. fMRI studies with younger children were excluded because they are scarce

span.label: all correlational analyses were dropped because the measures varied too much across studies
span.quote: All correlational analysis with other variables were not considered, given the variability in measures across studies.

span.label: the lateralization of the hippocampal response is stated to be unresolved in the literature
span.quote: The lateralization of the response in the hippocampus, however, has not been clarified in the literature.

span.label: the function of the insular and cingulate areas found for symbolic material is left for future work
span.quote: More studies should address the exact function of these areas both in calculation and numerical quantity processing.

span.label: TMS results are reported as not always consistent with the fMRI results they are compared to
span.quote: TMS has shown a role for both parietal lobes in processing quantity, including the left IPL ( Sandrini et al., 2004 ). Not all results were consistent with fMRI studies

span.label: an early attribution of simple-calculation errors to a spatial deficit is passed on with the note that it was argued without further explanation
span.quote: They argued, without further explanation, that they were related to the “general loss of automatisms” reported by Luria (1966)

span.label: the tripartite classification of acalculia, carried forward as the frame in which imaging results are read
span.quote: Observed acalculia was thus classified in three main categories ( Berger, 1926 ; Hécaen et al., 1961 ; Hécaen and Angelergues, 1961 ): (1) “primary acalculia” (“anarithmethia”), the disturbance of core math functions, resulting from lesions of the left parietal areas; (2) secondary acalculia, determined by language problems (mostly reading and writing disorders), resulting from lesions in left perisylvian, language-related, areas, and (3) secondary, “spatial” acalculia, following lesions of the posterior areas of the right hemisphere, related to spatial disorders, like, for instance, unilateral spatial neglect. In this classification, therefore, there was no primary role for the right hemisphere.

span.label: neuronal recycling - an area engaged for one purpose being progressively taken over for arithmetic during education
span.quote: Unlike for the IPS, the right PSPL is not considered to be specific to quantity-based processing, but to mechanisms of visuo-spatial attention, which might be progressively engaged or “recycled” in these tasks during arithmetic education

span.label: acalculia is not one deficit but a three-way classification - anarithmethia, language-secondary and spatial - whose members have different lesion sides, so a lesion-side claim about 'acalculia' is underspecified until the type is named
span.quote: Observed acalculia was thus classified in three main categories ( Berger, 1926 ; Hécaen et al., 1961 ; Hécaen and Angelergues, 1961 ): (1) “primary acalculia” (“anarithmethia”), the disturbance of core math functions, resulting from lesions of the left parietal areas; (2) secondary acalculia, determined by language problems (mostly reading and writing disorders), resulting from lesions in left perisylvian, language-related, areas, and (3) secondary, “spatial” acalculia, following lesions of the posterior areas of the right hemisphere, related to spatial disorders, like, for instance, unilateral spatial neglect. In this classification, therefore, there was no primary role for the right hemisphere.

span.label: the 1974 claim is bounded by its method: performance was measured with nonverbal readout and input restricted to the left visual field or left hand, so 'almost negligible' describes what that preparation could show
span.quote: tests for mathematical performance in the minor hemisphere with nonverbal readout and with the sensory input restricted to the left visual field or the left hand, indicate … that the capacity for calculation on the minor side is almost negligible. By manipulating marbles or dowel sticks, watching spots of light flashed to the left field and pointing with the left hand, … (split brain) patients may succeed in matching numbers or in adding one to numbers below 10, but they fail when required to add or subtract two or higher numbers and they fail also at the simplest tasks in multiplication and division.

span.label: laterality in children is not a property of the child but of the stimulus format - the same IPS is left-dominant for symbolic and right-dominant for non-symbolic material
span.quote: The data on quantity processing confirm that the parietal areas used by children for processing numerical quantity differ in lateralization for symbolic and non-symbolic stimuli, especially for the IPS: the left IPS is driving the process with symbolic numbers while the right IPS drives quantity processing when the stimuli are non-symbolic.

span.label: the right hemisphere's contribution is not generic spatial support but specific stored content: the layout for a particular operation, and the parsing of zero
span.quote: An important, perhaps the newest, result is that there is more than a simple difference along the verbal/spatial dimensions distinguishing the work of each hemisphere. Very specific arithmetical functions like remembering the spatial templates for complex operations, or processing of zero in complex numbers, are indeed sustained in specific right sided areas.

span.label: this is a review that also runs its own meta-analysis, and its inclusion criteria are chosen for homogeneity rather than coverage - the pooling rule is stated, which is what makes its disagreement with the earlier meta-analysis checkable
span.quote: Based on the literature compiled by those meta-analysis, homogeneity in the tasks and the concrete dependent measures of the studies is emphasized. First, the literature on quantity was split in two subsets, attending to the use of symbolic or non-symbolic material.

span.label: a laterality index here is computed on ALE values, so it inherits whatever the pooled coordinate set contained; it measures the literature as assembled, not the brain directly
span.quote: To examine the hemispheric asymmetries, the MATLAB script AveLI ( Matsuo et al., 2012 ; http://aveli.web.fc2.com ) was used. This program considers not only the extension in voxels falling within two masks (left and right hemisphere mask), but also the intensity of the ALE value in our case.

span.label: contradicts → Sperry (1974) and Sperry et al. (1969) - calculation as an almost exclusively left-hemisphere function
span.quote: Fifty years after Sperry’s article, the notions about brain laterality of calculation are radically changed.

span.label: extends → Triple Code Model (Dehaene, 1992; Dehaene and Cohen, 1995)
span.quote: However, after over a quarter of a century, it needs additions.

span.label: replicates → Escobar-Magariño et al. (2022) adult symbolic/non-symbolic IPS laterality pattern
span.quote: This pattern resembles the one recently reported by Escobar-Magariño et al. (2022) in adults.

span.label: extends → Arsalidou et al. (2018) meta-analysis of numerical development
span.quote: Thus, the overall right lateralization in children reported in previous meta-analyses (e.g., Arsalidou et al., 2018 ) have been influenced by the non-symbolic literature.

span.label: contradicts → Sperry's 1974 conclusion that the right hemisphere's contribution to calculation is limited to additions summing under 20
span.quote: In 1974, Roger Sperry, based on his seminal studies on the split-brain condition, concluded that math was almost exclusively sustained by the language dominant left hemisphere. The right hemisphere could perform additions up to sums less than 20, the only exception to a complete left hemisphere dominance.

span.label: explains-away → the overall right lateralization for number in children reported by previous meta-analyses
span.quote: Thus, the overall right lateralization in children reported in previous meta-analyses (e.g., Arsalidou et al., 2018 ) have been influenced by the non-symbolic literature.

span.label: extends → the Triple Code Model as a framework for locating math functions
span.quote: The TCM still constitutes a valid framework for the location of math functions. However, after over a quarter of a century, it needs additions.

span.label: builds-on → Escobar-Magarino 2022's adult meta-analysis of symbolic and non-symbolic IPS lateralization
span.quote: In a recent meta-analysis by Escobar-Magariño et al. (2022) lateralization indexes suggested a prevalent left IPS dominance when the stimuli were symbolic and a right IPS dominance when the stimuli where non-symbolic.

span.label: qualifies → the verbal-versus-spatial account of what distinguishes the two hemispheres in arithmetic
span.quote: An important, perhaps the newest, result is that there is more than a simple difference along the verbal/spatial dimensions distinguishing the work of each hemisphere. Very specific arithmetical functions like remembering the spatial templates for complex operations, or processing of zero in complex numbers, are indeed sustained in specific right sided areas.

span.label: critiques → the attribution of right-hemisphere simple-calculation errors to a general loss of automatisms
span.quote: They argued, without further explanation, that they were related to the “general loss of automatisms” reported by Luria (1966)

span.label: anarithmethia —part-of→ acalculia
span.quote: Observed acalculia was thus classified in three main categories ( Berger, 1926 ; Hécaen et al., 1961 ; Hécaen and Angelergues, 1961 ): (1) “primary acalculia” (“anarithmethia”), the disturbance of core math functions, resulting from lesions of the left parietal areas; (2) secondary acalculia, determined by language problems (mostly reading and writing disorders), resulting from lesions in left perisylvian, language-related, areas, and (3) secondary, “spatial” acalculia, following lesions of the posterior areas of the right hemisphere, related to spatial disorders, like, for instance, unilateral spatial neglect. In this classification, therefore, there was no primary role for the right hemisphere.

span.label: acalculia —distinct-from→ right hemisphere
span.quote: Observed acalculia was thus classified in three main categories ( Berger, 1926 ; Hécaen et al., 1961 ; Hécaen and Angelergues, 1961 ): (1) “primary acalculia” (“anarithmethia”), the disturbance of core math functions, resulting from lesions of the left parietal areas; (2) secondary acalculia, determined by language problems (mostly reading and writing disorders), resulting from lesions in left perisylvian, language-related, areas, and (3) secondary, “spatial” acalculia, following lesions of the posterior areas of the right hemisphere, related to spatial disorders, like, for instance, unilateral spatial neglect. In this classification, therefore, there was no primary role for the right hemisphere.

span.label: spatial acalculia —causes→ neglect
span.quote: In spatial acalculia patients are unable to respect the order and the position of digits in relation to each other; when the cause is neglect, one side of the calculation space is ignored.

span.label: insula —causes→ zero
span.quote: Reading aloud and writing on dictation multidigit numbers containing zero has also been found to be a right hemisphere specific function ( Benavides-Varela et al., 2016 ). Surprisingly, right hemisphere patients, who are free from language disorders, committed many errors in these tasks, and not in numbers that do not contain zero. No relation was found of such errors with neglect or with generic cognitive impairment. These errors seem to reveal the existence of a basic mechanism entailing parsing and the ability to set-up empty-slot structures required for processing zeros in complex numbers. As also confirmed in a subsequent study on a huge group of stroke patients ( Haupt et al., 2017 ), this ability can be located in the right insula and its surroundings.

span.label: carry —part-of→ multiplication
span.quote: For example, he added the carry to the leftmost side of the multiplicand, or of the partial product, or to the partial product in the row below. He seemed to know when and how the carry must be added but he clearly forgot where . The authors concluded that he was lacking knowledge of the visuo-spatial layout representation specific to multiplication, that is learned at school and guides written multiplication.

span.label: multiplication —contrasted-with→ addition
span.quote: No individual site was positive for both addition and multiplication. Errors therefore do not simply result from shortage of processing resources, which would have not provoked operation-specific deficits.

span.label: approximation —operationalised-as→ right hemisphere
span.quote: Disruption on right parietal areas provoked multiplication errors, mostly consisting in replacing the correct solution with another table solution (e.g., 8×3 = 32 or 8 × 3 = 16). The authors attributed this effect to the left hemisphere, where the retrieval of tables is supported, taking over the operation. In contrast, disruption of the left hemisphere resulted in approximation errors (e.g., 8 × 3 = 25). This would be due to the activity of the right hemisphere, where approximation takes place.

span.label: left hemisphere —contrasted-with→ right hemisphere
span.quote: Disruption on right parietal areas provoked multiplication errors, mostly consisting in replacing the correct solution with another table solution (e.g., 8×3 = 32 or 8 × 3 = 16). The authors attributed this effect to the left hemisphere, where the retrieval of tables is supported, taking over the operation. In contrast, disruption of the left hemisphere resulted in approximation errors (e.g., 8 × 3 = 25). This would be due to the activity of the right hemisphere, where approximation takes place.

span.label: symbolic —contrasted-with→ non-symbolic
span.quote: The data on quantity processing confirm that the parietal areas used by children for processing numerical quantity differ in lateralization for symbolic and non-symbolic stimuli, especially for the IPS: the left IPS is driving the process with symbolic numbers while the right IPS drives quantity processing when the stimuli are non-symbolic.

span.label: ALE —operationalised-as→ laterality indexes
span.quote: The non-symbolic quantity subset analysis showed suprathreshold ALE values in the bilateral superior parietal lobe and the right IPS. The laterality indexes show a clear right asymmetry in the IPS, the involvement of bilateral SPLs

span.label: Auditory-Verbal Code —operationalised-as→ retrieval of arithmetic facts
span.quote: Finally, the Verbal Word Frame ( Auditory-Verbal Code ) organizes numbers as word sequences, supporting counting. Importantly, it sustains the retrieval of arithmetic facts, which is achieved phonologically through rote verbal memory.

span.label: Arabic Code —part-of→ TCM
span.quote: A second numerical representation proposed by the TCM is the Visual Arabic Form (or Arabic Code ), which works in the recognition of Arabic digits. It is located in the occipito-temporal cortices.

span.label: TCM —same-as→ Triple Code Model
span.quote: Studies on lateralization conducted via neuroimaging have been mostly inspired by the Triple Code Model (TCM, Dehaene, 1992 ; Dehaene and Cohen, 1995 ), a theoretical framework encompassing three main numerical representations and the corresponding brain areas.

span.label: NFA —contrasted-with→ VWFA
span.quote: The specific site of the so-called Number Form Area (NFA) has been the object of several studies in contrast to the visual word form area (VWFA).

span.label: SNARC —operationalised-as→ mental number line
span.quote: One important aspect of numerical cognition addressed with only a few neuroimaging studies is that of the lateralization of the “mental number line,” a representation whereby, in left to right readers, small numbers are on the left and large numbers are on the right. The best demonstration of such representation is the so called SNARC (Spatial Numerical Association of Response Codes, Dehaene et al., 1993 ) effect: within a given interval, small numbers are responded faster with the left hand and larger numbers are responded faster with the right hand.

span.label: corpus callosum —causes→ magnitude comparison
span.quote: Cantlon et al. (2011) used fiber-based tractography to examine the relation between the integrity of the fibers of the corpus callosum connecting the left and right parietal lobes and performance on magnitude comparison tasks. Less integrity of these fibers was found in children compared with adults, with a correlation between integrity and the performance on the tasks.

span.label: DD —contrasted-with→ IPS
span.quote: In contrast, Michels et al. (2018) revealed increased activation in the left IPS, frontal cortex, and visual areas in DD during number processing, as well as functional hyperconnectivity in parietal, frontal, visual, and temporal regions. This finding has been attributed to compensatory mechanisms and the increment of cognitive control resources in DD

span.label: split-brain —operationalised-as→ left hemisphere
span.quote: In 1974, Roger Sperry, based on his seminal studies on the split-brain condition, concluded that math was almost exclusively sustained by the language dominant left hemisphere. The right hemisphere could perform additions up to sums less than 20, the only exception to a complete left hemisphere dominance.

span.label: TMS —contrasted-with→ fMRI
span.quote: TMS has shown a role for both parietal lobes in processing quantity, including the left IPL ( Sandrini et al., 2004 ). Not all results were consistent with fMRI studies

span.label: PSPL —distinct-from→ IPS
span.quote: Unlike for the IPS, the right PSPL is not considered to be specific to quantity-based processing, but to mechanisms of visuo-spatial attention, which might be progressively engaged or “recycled” in these tasks during arithmetic education

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The meta-analysis was performed with Ginger-Ale ( http://brainmap.org/ale/; Research Imaging Center of the University of Texas in San Antonio), which estimates the likelihood that at least one of the coordinates falls in the template stereotaxic space, in activation likelihood estimated (ALE) values.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: ALE maps were calculated with a corrected value of p < 0.001.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: Then, laterality indexes (LIs) were obtained from each of the two subsets.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The average age between studies was 10.67 y.o. (SD: 1.09) and the total number of participants was 128.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: The meta-analysis was performed with Ginger-Ale ( http://brainmap.org/ale/; Research Imaging Center of the University of Texas in San Antonio), which estimates the likelihood that at least one of the coordinates falls in the template stereotaxic space, in activation likelihood estimated (ALE) values. All the coordinates were transformed to the MNI space, considering the method used by the authors for normalization. Then the meta-analysis was conducted in the MNI space. ALE maps were calculated with a corrected value of p < 0.001.

span.label: statistics
span.quote: To examine the hemispheric asymmetries, the MATLAB script AveLI ( Matsuo et al., 2012 ; http://aveli.web.fc2.com ) was used. This program considers not only the extension in voxels falling within two masks (left and right hemisphere mask), but also the intensity of the ALE value in our case.

span.label: The authors' own meta-analysis of non-symbolic quantity tasks in school-age children found clusters in bilateral superior parietal lobe and in the right intraparietal sulcus, with the laterality index showing clear right asymmetry in the IPS.
span.quote: The non-symbolic quantity subset analysis showed suprathreshold ALE values in the bilateral superior parietal lobe and the right IPS.

span.label: For symbolic quantity tasks the intraparietal sulcus flipped to a left-hemisphere preponderance, while every other activated area was right dominant.
span.quote: Attending to the LIs, and clearly differing from the non-symbolic subset, the IPS showed a left hemisphere preponderance.

span.label: The same IPS region is therefore left-driven for symbolic numbers and right-driven for non-symbolic quantity in children, so parietal lateralization depends on stimulus format rather than on the numerical operation.
span.quote: The data on quantity processing confirm that the parietal areas used by children for processing numerical quantity differ in lateralization for symbolic and non-symbolic stimuli, especially for the IPS: the left IPS is driving the process with symbolic numbers while the right IPS drives quantity processing when the stimuli are non-symbolic.

span.label: For simple addition in children the meta-analysis returned a left-lateralized parietal cortex and SMA together with bilateral insula, IFG and MFG and a right occipital pole.
span.quote: As per exact calculation (addition), the ALE-maps show suprathreshold values in the right occipital pole, bilateral insula and IFG, bilateral MFG, the right middle cingulate cortex, the left SMA and the left parietal cortex only.

span.label: The overall right lateralization reported for children by earlier meta-analyses is an artefact of those analyses being dominated by non-symbolic studies.
span.quote: Thus, the overall right lateralization in children reported in previous meta-analyses (e.g., Arsalidou et al., 2018 ) have been influenced by the non-symbolic literature.

span.label: Developmentally, the right IPS encodes numerical magnitude from early life independently of age, experience or mathematical knowledge, whereas the left IPS is barely involved at first.
span.quote: In fact, the left IPS does not have a strong involvement in sustaining basic numerical abilities early in life, while the right IPS readily encodes numerical magnitude independently of the amount of experience, mathematical knowledge, or age.

span.label: The right hemisphere's contribution to arithmetic is not merely generic spatial support: it stores the operation-specific spatial layout for complex written procedures and, in the right insula, parses complex numbers containing zero.
span.quote: For example, the right parietal lobe seems to store the operation-specific spatial layout required for complex arithmetical procedures and areas like the right insula are necessary in parsing complex numbers containing zero.

span.label: THE ARTEFACT NAMED: the overall right lateralization for number in children reported by earlier meta-analyses is attributed to the non-symbolic studies in the pool
span.quote: Thus, the overall right lateralization in children reported in previous meta-analyses (e.g., Arsalidou et al., 2018 ) have been influenced by the non-symbolic literature.

span.label: splitting the child literature by stimulus format reverses the direction: the left IPS drives symbolic quantity processing and the right IPS drives non-symbolic
span.quote: The data on quantity processing confirm that the parietal areas used by children for processing numerical quantity differ in lateralization for symbolic and non-symbolic stimuli, especially for the IPS: the left IPS is driving the process with symbolic numbers while the right IPS drives quantity processing when the stimuli are non-symbolic.

span.label: the non-symbolic subset gave suprathreshold ALE values in bilateral superior parietal lobe and right IPS, with a clear right asymmetry in the IPS
span.quote: The non-symbolic quantity subset analysis showed suprathreshold ALE values in the bilateral superior parietal lobe and the right IPS. The laterality indexes show a clear right asymmetry in the IPS, the involvement of bilateral SPLs

span.label: in the symbolic subset the IPS was left-preponderant while every other area was right-dominant
span.quote: Attending to the LIs, and clearly differing from the non-symbolic subset, the IPS showed a left hemisphere preponderance. All the rest of areas showed a dominance for the right hemisphere

span.label: for addition the laterality indexes show a clear left dominance for the IPS, with a slight right tendency frontally
span.quote: As per exact calculation (addition), the ALE-maps show suprathreshold values in the right occipital pole, bilateral insula and IFG, bilateral MFG, the right middle cingulate cortex, the left SMA and the left parietal cortex only. LIs shows a clear left dominance for the IPS.

span.label: at school age the laterality pattern changes as a function of the numerical stimuli presented
span.quote: To summarize, the results indicate that, at school age, the laterality pattern changes as a function of the numerical stimuli presented. The use of non-symbolic stimuli in magnitude comparison tasks entails a clear involvement of the parietal areas in the right hemisphere. Tasks with number symbols instead, shift the laterality pattern with significantly stronger activation in the left IPS.

span.label: children show a more extended and less specialized network than adults
span.quote: Notably, children show a more extended and less specialized network.

span.label: INCLUSION CRITERIA STATED: the literature was split into symbolic and non-symbolic subsets to keep tasks and dependent measures homogeneous
span.quote: Based on the literature compiled by those meta-analysis, homogeneity in the tasks and the concrete dependent measures of the studies is emphasized. First, the literature on quantity was split in two subsets, attending to the use of symbolic or non-symbolic material.

span.label: the contrasts for negative numbers in one study were dropped, explicitly departing from the earlier meta-analysis, to increase homogeneity
span.quote: Differing from Arsalidou et al. (2018) , and again with the main goal of increasing homogeneity across studies, the contrasts for negative numbers in Gullick and Wolford (2013) were not included.

span.label: a right-hemisphere patient kept the multiplication procedure in words but placed the carry wrongly, losing only the spatial layout
span.quote: For example, he added the carry to the leftmost side of the multiplicand, or of the partial product, or to the partial product in the row below. He seemed to know when and how the carry must be added but he clearly forgot where . The authors concluded that he was lacking knowledge of the visuo-spatial layout representation specific to multiplication, that is learned at school and guides written multiplication.

span.label: right-hemisphere patients without language disorders erred on multidigit numbers containing zero and not on numbers without it
span.quote: Reading aloud and writing on dictation multidigit numbers containing zero has also been found to be a right hemisphere specific function ( Benavides-Varela et al., 2016 ). Surprisingly, right hemisphere patients, who are free from language disorders, committed many errors in these tasks, and not in numbers that do not contain zero. No relation was found of such errors with neglect or with generic cognitive impairment. These errors seem to reveal the existence of a basic mechanism entailing parsing and the ability to set-up empty-slot structures required for processing zeros in complex numbers. As also confirmed in a subsequent study on a huge group of stroke patients ( Haupt et al., 2017 ), this ability can be located in the right insula and its surroundings.

span.label: right-hemisphere patients without neglect still failed one-digit mental subtraction and multiplication, tasks needing no written visuospatial ability
span.quote: Right hemisphere patients without neglect still showed an impairment of math. Importantly, these patients failed in one-digit mental subtraction and multiplication, tasks that do not require written visuospatial abilities.

span.label: pure arithmetical errors outnumbered spatial ones, were associated with lower parietal lesions and were not predicted by visuo-spatial ability
span.quote: Interestingly, pure arithmetical errors (failure with number facts, carrying, borrowing, etc.) were more numerous than errors of spatial origin and were associated with lower parietal lesions; they were not predicted by visuo-spatial abilities. In contrast, spatial errors (misalignment, omissions of the left-most digits, number inversions, etc., often accompanied by neglect) were associated with lesions in fronto-temporoparietal areas; they were predicted by composite measures of visuo-spatial attentional and representational abilities.

span.label: disrupting the right parietal lobe produced table-substitution errors and disrupting the left produced approximation errors
span.quote: Disruption on right parietal areas provoked multiplication errors, mostly consisting in replacing the correct solution with another table solution (e.g., 8×3 = 32 or 8 × 3 = 16). The authors attributed this effect to the left hemisphere, where the retrieval of tables is supported, taking over the operation.
